translations.answer: Maintainer notes that the original post's WORLD Jacobian is applied at the world origin, which seems to be attached to LF_FOOT; it is not the intended center of the foot. LOCAL_WORLD_ALIGNED is applied at the LF_FOOT frame, with axes aligned to the world frame. The author used LOCAL_WORLD_ALIGNED and confirmed the force values are more reasonable. The original thread did not verify the rest of the assumptions regarding 3×3 matrix extraction, pseudoinverse, and peak torque mapping, so only the reference frame correction is confirmed, and results cannot be called strictly maximum contact force.
translations.applicability: Applies to the original post's LF_FOOT contact force coordinate explanation; other frames, points, and torque distribution require separate modeling.
translations.credibility.rationale: Environmental, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: The author changed the reference frame of computeFrameJacobian from WORLD to LOCAL_WORLD_ALIGNED.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: First, check if the Jacobian's reference frame matches the required point and axis direction.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Use LOCAL_WORLD_ALIGNED when the contact force mapping requires the center of the foot and world-aligned axes.
translations.details.environments.0: Pinocchio Python 2020; FreeFlyer quadruped; q0 is a unit base quaternion; LF_FOOT Jacobian.
translations.details.limits.0: The thread did not prove the 3×3 matrix is invertible, nor did it verify the pseudoinverse, other leg coupling, floating base balance, or friction constraints.
translations.details.limits.1: A more reasonable number does not equate to a strictly maximum feasible contact force.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The author confirmed the force values are more reasonable after changing the reference frame.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Why is one force component significantly larger than expected when estimating contact force from the foot Jacobian using peak joint torques?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Force torque limits and contact feasible region deployment must be verified under complete floating base dynamics and friction constraints before deployment.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The WORLD frame corresponds to the world origin, and is not centered and world-aligned at the LF_FOOT.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Using the WORLD frame, extracting a 3×3 Jacobian, and performing a pseudoinverse on J^T results in at least one x/y/z force component that is significantly larger than expected.
translations.source.locator: Issue #1292, maintainer reference frame diagnosis issuecomment-692582302; author re-measure issuecomment-692611643
translations.source.title: From the foot Jacobian and joint torques, how should WORLD and LOCAL_WORLD_ALIGNED be chosen?
